inflation_management: French Polynesia is a French collectivity using the CFP franc, pegged to the euro, so monetary conditions are set by the ECB via Paris; there is no IMF data series. Inflation tracks French and euro-area conditions plus very high import costs across a vast ocean territory. Tourism (Bora Bora, Moorea) and the black-pearl industry are the main private sectors, both highly cyclical - the pearl downturn after 2008 and the COVID tourism freeze were the period's big price-and-activity shocks.
debt_management: As a French collectivity, French Polynesia's public finances are backstopped by Paris through transfers that fund a large share of the budget. Local borrowing is modest and the fiscal risk sits with France, not Papeete. The economic structure - transfers plus tourism plus pearls - has barely changed in decades, which is both its stability and its stagnation.

key_events.event: Ongoing reckoning with the 1966-96 nuclear testing legacy at Moruroa, including compensation claims under France's Morin law.
COVID-19 shut down tourism, the main private-sector employer, before a strong 2022-23 rebound.
Pro-independence Tavini party won the territorial elections, reviving the autonomy debate with Paris.

outlook_next_decade: The status quo - French transfers plus tourism - is likely to persist; the independence question will simmer without near-term resolution. Tourism faces climate and cost pressures but the luxury brand is durable. The nuclear-legacy file will continue to shape relations with Paris. Expect stability, not transformation.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
